carousels.name: 4 reasons December is harder than November for quitting p*rn

slides.title: 4 reasons quitting p*rn gets [[harder in December]] — not easier.
slides.sub: Plan for it with 10 days still to go.

slides.title: Reasons [[1–2]]
items: No challenge. Nobody's counting with you anymore.
Holidays. Time off, travel, late nights — p*rn's favorite mix.

slides.title: Reasons [[3–4]]
items: The "I earned it" voice. 30 days feels like a reward is due.
Year-end stress. Deadlines, money, family — stress goes looking for p*rn.

slides.title: November was [[practice]]
slides.body: The challenge got you started. December is where quitting p*rn becomes your choice, not a trend.

slides.title: Your December [[plan]]
items: Set a new target: 60 days by New Year's.
Mark your risky dates on a calendar now.
Keep your blocker on through the holidays.
Find one person to count December with you.

carousels.name: 5 reasons p*rn feels normal to Gen Z (39% daily or weekly)

slides.title: 5 reasons p*rn feels normal [[to your generation.]]
slides.sub: 39% of Gen Z adults watch it daily or weekly.

slides.title: Daily or [[weekly]]
slides.body: A Barna / Pure Desire survey (2,976 U.S. adults, 2023) found 39% of Gen Z adults view p*rn daily or weekly. Overall, 61% of adults said they view it — up from 55% in 2015.

slides.title: Reasons [[1–3]]
items: It's one tap away — no effort, no cost.
Friends joke about it, so nobody takes it seriously.
Feeds keep serving softer versions all day.

slides.title: Reasons [[4–5]]
items: Nobody talks about the cost — sleep, focus, relationships.
Common feels harmless. But common isn't the same as fine.

slides.title: Be the [[exception]]
items: Count your p*rn-free days honestly.
Mute accounts that keep pulling you back.
Say it out loud: "I don't watch p*rn."
Talk about it with one friend — break the joke.

carousels.name: 5 reasons willpower alone won't beat p*rn addiction

slides.title: 5 reasons [[willpower alone]] won't beat your p*rn addiction.
slides.sub: Stop trying harder. Start trying smarter.

slides.title: It runs [[out]]
slides.body: Willpower is weakest at night, when you're tired — exactly when p*rn shows up. You're fighting at your worst hour.

slides.title: Reasons [[2–3]]
items: You keep the phone in bed and call it a test of strength.
You rely on mood, and mood changes every hour.

slides.title: Reasons [[4–5]]
items: You never fix the trigger, only the moment.
You do it alone — and p*rn loves alone.

slides.title: Use [[systems]] instead
items: Make p*rn hard to reach — block it on every device.
Your phone sleeps in the kitchen, not next to you.
Plan the 2 riskiest hours of your day.
Have one person you text when it hits.

Stop white-knuckling.

slides.lead: A p*rn blocker on every device, a panic button for weak moments and real people for accountability.

carousels.name: 5 ways to clean your feed of p*rn triggers

slides.title: 5 ways to clean your feed [[of p*rn triggers.]]
slides.sub: You quit p*rn. Your algorithm didn't.

slides.title: "Not interested", [[every time]]
slides.body: Long-press suggestive posts and tap "Not interested." The algorithm learns from what you skip, too.

slides.title: Ways [[2–3]]
items: Unfollow every account that's "almost" p*rn.
Search on purpose for sports, cooking, comedy — teach your feed a new taste.

slides.title: Ways [[4–5]]
items: Clear your search history in each app.
Turn off autoplay and skip the Explore page.

slides.title: Give it [[a week]]
slides.body: Feeds take a few days to change. Keep going. Fewer soft triggers means fewer p*rn urges you have to fight.

carousels.name: 8 questions your accountability partner should ask (NNN)

slides.title: 8 questions your accountability partner [[should ask you about p*rn.]]
Questions [[1–3]]
items: When was your last strong urge — and what did you do?
What time is p*rn hardest to resist right now?
Have you gone looking for "almost" p*rn?

slides.title: Questions [[4–6]]
items: How are you sleeping?
What are you stressed about this week?
Is there anything you haven't told me?

slides.title: Questions [[7–8]]
items: What's your plan for the riskiest night this week?
What's one win you're proud of?

slides.title: Make it [[work]]
items: Send them this list today.
Pick a fixed time — same day every week.
Answer honestly about p*rn, even when it's awkward.
Ask them back — it works both ways.
